evidence.content:
actions that affect organizational workflows. We describe a local AI workbench integrating workspace-scoped
document retrieval, a deterministic evidence threshold, persisted task execution and owner approval for a report tool.
The implementation uses a Go API, Python AI service, PostgreSQL/pgvector, object storage and a locally configured
model endpoint. Its planner implements a bounded search/report sequence rather than a general autonomous agent.
We analyze retained local validation and conduct an additional controlled generation pilot. A historical
authenticated-read workload completed 80,000 requests without observed errors and reached a peak of 2,823.4
requests/s at 50 concurrent clients. A separate 12-task model workload recorded a 25.12-second p95 latency. An

earlier three-question pilot achieved complete expected-keyword coverage, a measure that does not establish answer
accuracy. In 24 fixed-evidence generations across two local models and two temperatures, all calls succeeded, but
one high-temperature output adopted an unsupported deletion premise from adversarial evidence. The results
demonstrate a functioning local workflow and the need to distinguish retrieval signal, text faithfulness and action
authorization. Small datasets, incomplete historical configuration capture and unblinded exploratory review limit
generalization. We provide source/evidence hashes, raw pilot outputs and a protocol for broader evaluation.

Keywords: retrieval-augmented generation; local inference; evidence gating; human approval; workspace isolation;

prompt injection; systems evaluation.

Appendix B. Minimal replication protocol

Use the existing local models and execute source/run_model_pilot.py. Its requests use two temperatures, two seeds,
three fixed cases and a per-model warmup, saving all outputs as JSON. A rerun requires fresh review of responses; do
not reuse manual labels automatically. Record model digests rather than aliases alone, preserve the runtime version
and distinguish wall time from server-reported generation duration.

For an end-to-end comparison, create an isolated workspace per variant, ingest an identical versioned corpus with one
fixed embedder, prevent prior generated memories from contaminating later trials and run the same questions through
the authenticated task API. A model-only generation pilot is insufficient to measure retrieval or authorization effects.

For an embedding comparison, rebuild the corpus embeddings and recalibrate on a development split before
evaluating the held-out questions.

8. Threats to validity and responsible use

Internal validity is limited by missing historical revision/digest metadata, non-isolated local resources, sequential
stage/model order and differences between the native model pilot and application endpoint. The quality pilot predates
a retrieval-evidence fix, so its scores cannot be treated as final-revision quality evidence. New pilot prompts omitted

application memory to isolate supplied-evidence generation, which also limits ecological validity.

Construct validity is limited by keyword coverage and citation-marker checks. A keyword can appear in irrelevant
evidence; a citation marker can point to a passage that does not entail a claim. The post-hoc pilot rubric was applied
by the documentation authoring assistant without blinding or independent expert agreement. It is useful for explaining
these particular outputs, not a validated measurement instrument.

External validity is limited by a three-file synthetic corpus, a repeated AI load question, six calls per model-temperature
cell and only two injection trials in each cell. Neither zero observed API errors nor three complete keyword-hit fractions

generalizes to arbitrary users, languages, domains or workloads. No public deployment, field-user benefit study or
long-duration model soak was recorded.

Statistical validity is limited by single load stages and tiny model samples. We report denominators and raw values
rather than significance tests or population-level confidence claims. The 1/2 contamination count in one cell is not a
stable estimate of attack success probability. Token length and cache effects confound model latency comparisons.

The evaluation inputs are synthetic maintenance statements; no private operational corpus was needed for the added
experiments. The bundle omits environment secrets and database dumps and records a redaction in a copied
development log.

Each made 20,000 requests: 75% workspace collection reads and 25% authenticated-profile reads. The same QA
identity and small dataset were used. Throughput is request count divided by elapsed stage time. Per-request latency
excludes executor waiting before a worker starts the call, and percentiles use nearest-rank selection. Acceptance was
zero errors and p95 below 2 seconds at each stage.

4.4 AI workload and earlier keyword pilot

A separate AI stress record contains 12 tasks at concurrency three using one repeated maintenance question, with
task completion/evidence/citation checks. It contains no independently graded answer rubric. The earlier
three-question evaluation uses expected keywords and counts a hit if a keyword occurs in either evidence or answer;

its mean is an average of per-question hit fractions. This is a keyword coverage heuristic, despite broader language in
the evaluator's docstring.

4.5 Additional model and temperature pilot

We ran two installed tags, qwen:7b and gemma:7b, at temperatures 0.0 and 0.8 on three cases, using seeds 17 and
29. Cases asked for a bearing/date, an absent repair cost, and a filter incident accompanied by adversarial deletion
instructions. The 24 serial measured calls followed one excluded warmup per model, with shuffled order within each
model. Qwen's block preceded Gemma's; order across models was not counterbalanced.
